properties.statement:
ROOT-CAUSE PASS ON DANGLING NODE REFERENCES, 2026-08-29, run under the root-cause skill after three separate sessions had COUNTED them (7 on 08-16, 9 on 08-26, 9 on 08-29) and none had asked why they arise.

═══ ① WHY THE NINE EXISTED — TWO CAUSES, NOT ONE, AND NEITHER IS A RENAME ═══

Split by asking whether the SLUG exists under a different prefix:

    6 of 9  PREFIX ERROR ON A REAL SLUG    5 x prj:reflow2 -> proj:reflow2
                                           1 x cap:thin-install -> req:thin-install
    3 of 9  CONSTRUCTED FROM A TOOL NAME   cap:reconcile-artifacts, cap:link-artifacts,
                                           cap:gap-to-prompt — slug exists NOWHERE, and all
                                           three are the names of SERVED TOOLS
                                           (reconcile_artifacts, link_artifact, gap_to_prompt)

⭐ ONE MECHANISM UNDER BOTH: THE ID WAS CONSTRUCTED BY CONVENTION RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY LOOKUP. One group gets the prefix wrong, the other invents a slug from the tool it just used, assuming a capability is named after the tool that serves it. Neither involved asking the graph. That confirms and generalises the cause already recorded on `fact:nine-temporalfacts-point-their-subject-at-a-node-that-does-not-exist` for five of them — *"the agent read an existing fact, copied its subject_id convention, and never checked that the id resolved"*.

═══ ② THE CLASS IS NOT 'POINTERS ARE UNGUARDED'. IT IS THAT THE JUDGEMENT WAS MADE ONCE. ═══

`heal.rs` names three properties that carry a node as a value rather than as an edge. Measured across all of them on this graph:

    TemporalFact.subject_id   333 values, 333 resolve   declared node_ref: YES
    Snapshot.target_id        195 values, 191 resolve   declared node_ref: NO
    Question.gap_id            57 values,   0 resolve   declared node_ref: NO

🛑 AND THE THREE NEED THREE DIFFERENT ANSWERS, which is why this is a judgement and not something to automate:

• `subject_id` — a fact ABOUT a node. If the node goes, the fact is about nothing. Dangling is a REAL DEFECT. Correctly declared.
• `Snapshot.target_id` — a snapshot OF a node at an epoch. If the node is later deleted, THE SNAPSHOT IS THE ONLY SURVIVING RECORD OF IT. Dangling here is the mechanism WORKING. Declaring it would make a detector fire on correct history. Correctly undeclared — but nothing anywhere says so.
• `Question.gap_id` — names a COMPUTED gap, never a node. 0 of 57 resolve and that is right. Not a node reference at all. Correctly undeclared — and again nothing says so.

⚠️ SO THE DEFECT IS THE UNRECORDED JUDGEMENT, NOT THE MISSING FLAG. `subject_id` and `target_id` are declared IDENTICALLY in the schema — `type: string, required: true, indexed: true` — and differ only in `node_ref`. Nothing states why. The next person to notice the asymmetry has exactly two moves: declare it, and get a detector firing on correct history; or leave it, and never learn that the omission was deliberate. Both are worse than the judgement being written down.

═══ ③ THE RETIRE CASE IS REAL AFTER ALL — IT WAS JUST IN THE PROPERTY NOBODY SWEPT ═══

Earlier the same day this session withdrew the 'rename' leg from `dec:a-restore-reports-an-unresolvable-reference-rather-than-refusing-it`, on the measured ground that all nine `subject_id` dangles were wrong WHEN WRITTEN and none came from a retire. That is true of `subject_id` and it was too broad. All four `Snapshot.target_id` dangles are retires:

    art:content, art:content-test, art:tools-content   snapshotted at epoch:content-store-discontinued
    ctr:anthony                                        snapshotted at epoch:the-owners-identity-is-one-node-again

Every one resolved when written and broke when its target was deleted or merged. `fact:defect-seven-temporal-facts-name-a-subject-id-that-does-not-exist` (2026-08-16) predicted exactly this and said so — *"NOT ESTABLISHED: whether Snapshot.target_id and Question.gap_id carry the same rot. Nobody has swept them"* — and thirteen days later nobody had.

🛑 NOT MEASURED, so this is not read wider than it is: only this one graph, and only the three properties `heal.rs` already names. Whether other node types carry undeclared de facto pointers was not swept — a scan for string values matching an id shape found only these three plus `Artifact.checksum` and `DesignEpoch.checksum`, which match on the `sha256:` prefix and are not references.
